seoTitle: How to Make Instagram Reels With Canva (2026)
metaDescription: Build an Instagram Reel in Canva from a clip, a text hook and template scenes, then post it. Includes the 60-second cap on sharing from Canva to Instagram and why you can't schedule Reels there.
intro:
A Reel in Canva is a short timeline of clips, text overlays and template scenes. Build one and the pattern repeats for every Reel after it. This guide follows a real build: a single vertical clip, a text hook on top, a second scene borrowed from a template, and the assembled timeline.

The last step is where most guides go vague. Canva can post straight to Instagram, but only videos between 3 and 60 seconds, and it can't schedule Reels at all. Instagram itself accepts Reels up to 20 minutes. Knowing which route your video fits saves a failed upload.

tables.title: Posting from Canva vs uploading in Instagram
rows: Up to 20 minutes; Reels over 3 minutes aren't recommended to new audiences
Set by your Canva design (Instagram Reel is 1080 × 1920)
tables.note: From Canva's sharing-limitations page and Instagram's Help Center, checked September 2026. Canva also caps direct sharing at 25 uploads per 24 hours per Instagram business account.

steps.heading: Start with your base clip in an Instagram Reel design
steps.body:
Start from an Instagram Reel template or design, which Canva sizes at 1080 × 1920 pixels (9:16). Drop a vertical clip onto the canvas and the timeline appears underneath, with the clip's frames stretched across a track you can trim from either end. Here the clip runs 15 seconds.

Because the canvas is already Reel-shaped, what you see in the editor is what followers will see in the feed.

image.caption: A vertical video clip loaded into Canva's Reel editor, with the timeline and clip thumbnails visible below the preview.

steps.heading: Put a short hook on screen
steps.body:
Text laid over the footage is what turns a plain clip into a Reel. In this build a bold serif line, "3 Ways To Grows", sits in the centre with a smaller "Business Tip" label above and a byline below, all taken from a template's existing text styles.

Keep the hook short enough to read in a second or two. That's the window a scrolling viewer gives you.

image.caption: A bold text overlay added over the base video clip, the hook text that turns raw footage into a scroll-stopping opener.

steps.heading: Add a second scene from Templates
steps.body:
Open the Templates panel mid-project and pick a scene to drop in as a new segment, like this "Flash Sale Alert!" layout. The panel shows the template's size (Instagram Reel, 1080 × 1920 px), its font pairing (Barlow with Lobster) and a More like this row for scenes in the same style. Pulling scenes from one family keeps a multi-scene Reel from looking stitched together.

When a clip is selected, the toolbar above the canvas also offers Captions, Speed, Slip and Animate. BG Remover carries a crown, which marks it as a Pro feature.

image.caption: Browsing template scenes to add as a new segment, here a Flash Sale announcement layout with matching fonts and "More like this" suggestions.

steps.heading: Assemble and trim the timeline
steps.body:
Clips and scenes line up left to right along the bottom, each with its own duration bar. Text sits on separate tracks above the video, so you can trim or move it without touching the footage. This build totals 48 seconds.

Play the whole thing through before exporting. Look for a scene that lingers, text that doesn't clear before the next clip, or a jarring jump in style. Put the strongest visual first. Dead air in the middle loses viewers before they reach the call to action.

image.caption: The assembled Reel timeline with multiple clips and text tracks stacked together, 48 seconds in total.

steps.heading: Post it to Instagram
steps.body:
If the Reel is between 3 and 60 seconds, click Share, then See all, choose Instagram, and connect your account the first time. You can't schedule it. Instagram doesn't allow Reels or Stories to be scheduled through Canva, so it publishes when you share. On a phone, the Canva mobile app can hand the Reel to Instagram if both apps are installed.

For anything longer than 60 seconds, click Share, then Download, choose MP4 Video, and upload the file in Instagram yourself. There's no Instagram-specific export preset in Canva: the Reel shape comes from the design size, and the file is a standard MP4 at 1080p by default. In the Instagram app, turn on Upload at highest quality (Profile, Menu, Media quality) so Instagram doesn't compress it further.

troubleshooting.problem: Sharing to Instagram from Canva fails
troubleshooting.cause: The video is under 3 seconds, over 60 seconds, or larger than 100 MB, or the account has hit 25 uploads in 24 hours.
troubleshooting.fix: Trim it to 60 seconds or less, or download the MP4 and upload it in Instagram, which accepts Reels up to 20 minutes.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no option to schedule the Reel
troubleshooting.cause: Instagram doesn't allow Reels or Stories to be scheduled through Canva's Content Planner. Only single image or video feed posts can be scheduled, and only from an Instagram Business account linked to a Facebook page.
troubleshooting.fix: Post the Reel when you want it live, or download it and use Instagram's own tools.

faq.question: How long can a Reel made in Canva be?
faq.answer: Canva will share videos of 3 to 60 seconds straight to Instagram. Instagram accepts Reels up to 20 minutes if you upload them yourself, but it won't recommend Reels over 3 minutes to new audiences.

faq.question: Can I combine my own clips with Canva templates?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with your footage, then add template scenes from the Templates panel as extra segments on the same timeline.

faq.question: Can I schedule an Instagram Reel from Canva?
faq.answer: No. Instagram doesn't allow Reels to be scheduled through Canva. Content Planner scheduling covers single image or video feed posts, needs Canva Pro, Teams or Nonprofits, and needs an Instagram Business account linked to a Facebook page.

faq.question: What resolution should I export?
faq.answer: MP4 at the default 1080p in a 1080 × 1920 design. Instagram's minimum is 720p at 30 frames per second, and Canva Free users can only download at the default quality.

Sharing limits, scheduling rules and download options were re-checked against Canva's help center, and Reel length and size rules against Instagram's Help Center, in September 2026. That check removed this guide's earlier reference to a Canva "Instagram Reel export preset" (the export is a standard MP4; the Reel shape comes from the design size) and added the 60-second, 100 MB cap on sharing from Canva to Instagram.
